title: Rules as Code Research
body:
At Michigan Technological University I am also involved in research, working in Dr. Wallace's research program on the ability to describe statutory rules using formal models. This work looks at how to convey the implications of rules to stakeholders, both those who are affected by them and those who write them.

I received SURF and URIP grant funding from Michigan Technological University to support this work, and have built a model using the Alloy specification language, taking advantage of Alloy's temporal modelling to determine how systems may change over time and how rules can enforce those changes.

To make the research accessible beyond the formal model itself, I built a full-stack application with a Spring Boot Java backend, Angular frontend, and MongoDB database, giving stakeholders an interface to interact with the Alloy model and see how rule changes affect real outcomes, such as student registration and graduation requirements.

This work has been presented at Michigan Tech's research symposium and was recognized with the Audience Choice Award at the 2026 Undergraduate Research Symposium.
